label: USE CASE 18
title: How Self Driving Cars See the Road

scenes.text: A car drives through traffic, with nobody touching the steering wheel. [1] It sees lanes, signals, bikes and people, and decides what to do, many times every second. [2] Let's break down how self driving cars see the road.

Every moment, the car runs a loop. [1] Sensors capture the world, cameras, radar, and sometimes lidar. [2] Perception models detect cars, lanes, signs and people. [3] Prediction models guess what everyone will do next, like that biker turning left. [4] A planner picks the safest path and speed, [5] and control turns it into steering, braking and acceleration.

Each sensor has a job. [1] Cameras see colour, signs and lane markings. [2] Radar measures distance and speed, even in fog or rain. [3] Lidar uses lasers to build a precise 3D map. [4] And GPS, with maps, tells the car where it is.

data.heading: The sensors
terms: Distance and speed, even in fog

scenes.text: The car combines all these sensors, and that's called sensor fusion. [1] Each sensor covers another's weaknesses. [2] Cameras can struggle with glare, [3] radar can't read signs, [4] but together, they build one reliable picture.

data.definition: Combining cameras, radar and other sensors into one reliable picture of the road.

scenes.text: Self driving comes in levels. [1] Driver assistance, like lane keeping and adaptive cruise control, where you're still driving. [2] Partial self driving, where the car steers and brakes, but you must watch constantly. [3] And full self driving, with no driver needed, which today runs as robotaxis in only a few cities.

data.heading: Levels of autonomy
steps: No driver, robotaxis in a few cities

scenes.text: So why is it so hard, especially on Indian roads? [1] Unpredictable traffic, like cows, autos, and people crossing anywhere. [2] Missing or faded lane markings. [3] And heavy rain, with poor visibility.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think today's cars with autopilot features can drive themselves anywhere. [2] Most cars sold today only have driver assistance. You must keep your hands ready, and your eyes on the road.

data.myth: Cars with autopilot features can drive themselves anywhere.
data.fact: Most cars today only have driver assistance. Hands ready, eyes on the road.
